NASB.1: 'Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, with all his people came out to meet us in battle at Edrei.
NASB.2: 'But the LORD said to me, 'Do not fear him, for I have delivered him and all his people and his land into your hand; and you shall do to him just as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.'
NASB.3: 'So the LORD our God delivered Og also, king of Bashan, with all his people into our hand, and we smote them until no survivor was left.
NASB.4: 'We captured all his cities at that time; there was not a city which we did not take from them: sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
NASB.5: 'All these were cities fortified with high walls, gates and bars, besides a great many unwalled towns.
NASB.6: 'We utterly destroyed them, as we did to Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women and children of every city.
NASB.7: 'But all the animals and the spoil of the cities we took as our booty.
NASB.8: 'Thus we took the land at that time from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the valley of Arnon to Mount Hermon
NASB.9: (Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir):
NASB.10: all the cities of the plateau and all Gilead and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
NASB.11: (For only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. Behold, his bedstead was an iron bedstead; it is in Rabbah of the sons of Ammon. Its length was nine cubits and its width four cubits by ordinary cubit.)
NASB.12: 'So we took possession of this land at that time. From Aroer, which is by the valley of Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead and its cities I gave to the Reubenites and to the Gadites.
NASB.13: 'The rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh, all the region of Argob (concerning all Bashan, it is called the land of Rephaim.
NASB.14: Jair the son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and called it, [that is], Bashan, after his own name, Havvoth-jair, [as it is] to this day.)
NASB.16: 'To the Reubenites and to the Gadites I gave from Gilead even as far as the valley of Arnon, the middle of the valley as a border and as far as the river Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon;
NASB.17: the Arabah also, with the Jordan as [a] border, from Chinnereth even as far as the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, at the foot of the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
NASB.18: 'Then I commanded you at that time, saying, 'The LORD your God has given you this land to possess it; all you valiant men shall cross over armed before your brothers, the sons of Israel.
NASB.19: 'But your wives and your little ones and your livestock (I know that you have much livestock) shall remain in your cities which I have given you,
NASB.20: until the LORD gives rest to your fellow countrymen as to you, and they also possess the land which the LORD your God will give them beyond the Jordan. Then you may return every man to his possession which I have given you.'
NASB.21: 'I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, 'Your eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings; so the LORD shall do to all the kingdoms into which you are about to cross.
NASB.22: 'Do not fear them, for the LORD your God is the one fighting for you.'
NASB.23: 'I also pleaded with the LORD at that time, saying,
NASB.24: 'O Lord GOD, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand; for what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do such works and mighty acts as Yours?
NASB.25: 'Let me, I pray, cross over and see the fair land that is beyond the Jordan, that good hill country and Lebanon.'
NASB.26: 'But the LORD was angry with me on your account, and would not listen to me; and the LORD said to me, 'Enough! Speak to Me no more of this matter.
NASB.27: 'Go up to the top of Pisgah and lift up your eyes to the west and north and south and east, and see [it] with your eyes, for you shall not cross over this Jordan.
NASB.28: 'But charge Joshua and encourage him and strengthen him, for he shall go across at the head of this people, and he will give them as an inheritance the land which you will see.'
NASB.29: 'So we remained in the valley opposite Beth-peor.

NKJV.1: “Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan; and Og king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.
NKJV.2: And the LORD said to me, ‘Do not fear him, for I have delivered him and all his people and his land into your hand; you shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Heshbon.’
NKJV.3: “So the LORD our God also delivered into our hands Og king of Bashan, with all his people, and we attacked him until he had no survivors remaining.
NKJV.4: And we took all his cities at that time; there was not a city which we did not take from them: sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
NKJV.5: All these cities were fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides a great many rural towns.
NKJV.6: And we utterly destroyed them, as we did to Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children of every city.
NKJV.7: But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as booty for ourselves.
NKJV.8: “And at that time we took the land from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were on this side of the Jordan, from the River Arnon to Mount Hermon
NKJV.9: (the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir),
NKJV.10: all the cities of the plain, all Gilead, and all Bashan, as far as Salcah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
NKJV.11: “For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the giants. Indeed his bedstead was an iron bedstead. (Is it not in Rabbah of the people of Ammon?) Nine cubits is its length and four cubits its width, according to the standard cubit.
NKJV.12: “And this land, which we possessed at that time, from Aroer, which is by the River Arnon, and half the mountains of Gilead and its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites.
NKJV.13: The rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to half the tribe of Manasseh. (All the region of Argob, with all Bashan, was called the land of the giants.
NKJV.14: Jair the son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maachathites, and called Bashan after his own name, Havoth Jair, to this day.)
NKJV.16: And to the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave from Gilead as far as the River Arnon, the middle of the river as the border, as far as the River Jabbok, the border of the people of Ammon;
NKJV.17: the plain also, with the Jordan as the border, from Chinnereth as far as the east side of the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea), below the slopes of Pisgah.
NKJV.18: “Then I commanded you at that time, saying: ‘The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All you men of valor shall cross over armed before your brethren, the children of Israel.
NKJV.19: But your wives, your little ones, and your livestock (I know that you have much livestock) shall stay in your cities which I have given you,
NKJV.20: until the LORD has given rest to your brethren as to you, and they also possess the land which the LORD your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return to his possession which I have given you.’
NKJV.21: “And I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, ‘Your eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings; so will the LORD do to all the kingdoms through which you pass.
NKJV.22: You must not fear them, for the LORD your God Himself fights for you.’
NKJV.23: “Then I pleaded with the LORD at that time, saying:
NKJV.24: ‘O Lord GOD, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your mighty hand, for what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do anything like Your works and Your mighty deeds?
NKJV.25: I pray, let me cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan, those pleasant mountains, and Lebanon.’
NKJV.26: “But the LORD was angry with me on your account, and would not listen to me. So the LORD said to me: ‘Enough of that! Speak no more to Me of this matter.
NKJV.27: Go up to the top of Pisgah, and lift your eyes toward the west, the north, the south, and the east; behold it with your eyes, for you shall not cross over this Jordan.
NKJV.28: But command Joshua, and encourage him and strengthen him; for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which you will see.’
NKJV.29: “So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth Peor.

ESV.1: “Then we turned and went up the way to Bashan. And Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.
ESV.2: But the LORD said to me, ‘Do not fear him, for I have given him and all his people and his land into your hand. And you shall do to him as you did to Sihon the king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.’
ESV.3: So the LORD our God gave into our hand Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people, and we struck him down until he had no survivor left.
ESV.4: And we took all his cities at that time — there was not a city that we did not take from them — sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
ESV.5: All these were cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides very many unwalled villages.
ESV.6: And we devoted them to destruction,  as we did to Sihon the king of Heshbon, devoting to destruction every city, men, women, and children.
ESV.7: But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as our plunder.
ESV.8: So we took the land at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the Valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon
ESV.9: (the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, while the Amorites call it Senir),
ESV.10: all the cities of the tableland and all Gilead and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
ESV.11: (For only Og the king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. Behold, his bed was a bed of iron. Is it not in Rabbah of the Ammonites? Nine cubits  was its length, and four cubits its breadth, according to the common cubit. )
ESV.12: “When we took possession of this land at that time, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites the territory beginning at Aroer, which is on the edge of the Valley of the Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead with its cities.
ESV.13: The rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, that is, all the region of Argob, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh. (All that portion of Bashan is called the land of Rephaim.
ESV.14: Jair the Manassite took all the region of Argob, that is, Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and called the villages after his own name, Havvoth-jair, as it is to this day.)
ESV.16: and to the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the territory from Gilead as far as the Valley of the Arnon, with the middle of the valley as a border, as far over as the river Jabbok, the border of the Ammonites;
ESV.17: the Arabah also, with the Jordan as the border, from Chinnereth as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
ESV.18: “And I commanded you at that time, saying, ‘The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your men of valor shall cross over armed before your brothers, the people of Israel.
ESV.19: Only your wives, your little ones, and your livestock (I know that you have much livestock) shall remain in the cities that I have given you,
ESV.20: until the LORD gives rest to your brothers, as to you, and they also occupy the land that the LORD your God gives them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return to his possession which I have given you.’
ESV.21: And I commanded Joshua at that time, ‘Your eyes have seen all that the LORD your God has done to these two kings. So will the LORD do to all the kingdoms into which you are crossing.
ESV.22: You shall not fear them, for it is the LORD your God who fights for you.’
ESV.23: “And I pleaded with the LORD at that time, saying,
ESV.24: ‘O Lord GOD, you have only begun to show your servant your greatness and your mighty hand. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do such works and mighty acts as yours?
ESV.25: Please let me go over and see the good land beyond the Jordan, that good hill country and Lebanon.’
ESV.26: But the LORD was angry with me because of you and would not listen to me. And the LORD said to me, ‘Enough from you; do not speak to me of this matter again.
ESV.27: Go up to the top of Pisgah and lift up your eyes westward and northward and southward and eastward, and look at it with your eyes, for you shall not go over this Jordan.
ESV.28: But charge Joshua, and encourage and strengthen him, for he shall go over at the head of this people, and he shall put them in possession of the land that you shall see.’
ESV.29: So we remained in the valley opposite Beth-peor.

CSB17.1: “Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan, and King Og of Bashan <sup>ⓘ</sup> came out against us with his whole army to do battle at Edrei. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.2: But the LORD said to me, ‘Do not fear him, for I have handed him over to you along with his whole army and his land. Do to him as you did to King Sihon of the Amorites, <sup>ⓚ</sup> who lived in Heshbon.’
CSB17.3: So the LORD our God also handed over King Og of Bashan and his whole army to us. We struck him until there was no survivor left. <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.4: We captured all his cities at that time. There wasn’t a city that we didn’t take from them: sixty cities, the entire region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
CSB17.5: All these were fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides a large number of rural villages.
CSB17.6: We completely destroyed them, as we had done to King Sihon of Heshbon, destroying the men, women, and children of every city.
CSB17.7: But we took all the livestock and the spoil from the cities as plunder for ourselves. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.8: “At that time we took the land from the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, <sup>ⓝ</sup> from the Arnon Valley as far as Mount Hermon,
CSB17.9: which the Sidonians call Sirion, but the Amorites call Senir,
CSB17.10: all the cities of the plateau, Gilead, and Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of Og’s kingdom in Bashan. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.11: (Only King Og of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. <sup>ⓑ</sup> His bed <sup>[1]</sup> was made of iron. Isn’t it in Rabbah of the Ammonites? <sup>ⓒ</sup> It is 13½ feet long and 6 feet wide by a standard measure. <sup>[2]</sup>) <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.12: “At that time we took possession of this land. <sup>ⓔ</sup> I gave to the Reubenites and Gadites the area extending from Aroer by the Arnon Valley, and half the hill country of Gilead along with its cities.
CSB17.13: I gave to half the tribe of Manasseh the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og. The entire region of Argob, the whole territory of Bashan, used to be called the land of the Rephaim.
CSB17.14: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took over the entire region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites. He called Bashan by his own name, Jair’s Villages, <sup>[3]</sup> as it is today.
CSB17.16: and I gave to the Reubenites and Gadites the area extending from Gilead to the Arnon Valley (the middle of the valley was the border) and up to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
CSB17.17: The Arabah and Jordan are also borders from Chinnereth <sup>[4]</sup> as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Dead Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah on the east. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.18: “I commanded you at that time: The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your valiant men will cross over in battle formation ahead of your brothers the Israelites.
CSB17.19: But your wives, dependents, and livestock — I know that you have a lot of livestock — will remain in the cities I have given you <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.20: until the LORD gives rest <sup>ⓗ</sup> to your brothers as he has to you, and they also take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan. Then each of you may return to his possession that I have given you. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.21: “I commanded Joshua at that time: Your own eyes have seen everything the LORD your God has done to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you are about to enter.
CSB17.22: Don’t be afraid of them, for the LORD your God fights for you.
CSB17.23: “At that time I begged the LORD:
CSB17.24: Lord GOD, you have begun to show your greatness and your strong hand to your servant, for what god is there in heaven or on earth who can perform deeds and mighty acts like yours?
CSB17.25: Please let me cross over and see the beautiful land <sup>ⓙ</sup> on the other side of the Jordan, that good hill country and Lebanon.
CSB17.26: “But the LORD was angry with me because of you <sup>[5]</sup> and would not listen to me. The LORD said to me, ‘That’s enough! Do not speak to me again about this matter.
CSB17.27: Go to the top of Pisgah and look to the west, north, south, and east, and see it with your own eyes, for you will not cross the Jordan. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.28: But commission Joshua and encourage and strengthen him, for he will cross over ahead of the people and enable them to inherit this land that you will see.’ <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.29: So we stayed in the valley facing Beth-peor.

NLT.1: “Next we turned and headed for the land of Bashan, where King Og and his entire army attacked us at Edrei.
NLT.2: But the LORD told me, ‘Do not be afraid of him, for I have given you victory over Og and his entire army, and I will give you all his land. Treat him just as you treated King Sihon of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon.’
NLT.3: “So the LORD our God handed King Og and all his people over to us, and we killed them all. Not a single person survived.
NLT.4: We conquered all sixty of his towns — the entire Argob region in his kingdom of Bashan. Not a single town escaped our conquest.
NLT.5: These towns were all fortified with high walls and barred gates. We also took many unwalled villages at the same time.
NLT.6: We completely destroyed the kingdom of Bashan, just as we had destroyed King Sihon of Heshbon. We destroyed all the people in every town we conquered — men, women, and children alike.
NLT.7: But we kept all the livestock for ourselves and took plunder from all the towns.
NLT.8: “So we took the land of the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River — all the way from the Arnon Gorge to Mount Hermon.
NLT.9: (Mount Hermon is called Sirion by the Sidonians, and the Amorites call it Senir.)
NLT.10: We had now conquered all the cities on the plateau and all Gilead and Bashan, as far as the towns of Salecah and Edrei, which were part of Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
NLT.11: (King Og of Bashan was the last survivor of the giant Rephaites. His bed was made of iron and was more than thirteen feet long and six feet wide. It can still be seen in the Ammonite city of Rabbah.)
NLT.12: “When we took possession of this land, I gave to the tribes of Reuben and Gad the territory beyond Aroer along the Arnon Gorge, plus half of the hill country of Gilead with its towns.
NLT.13: Then I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan — Og’s former kingdom — to the half-tribe of Manasseh. (This entire Argob region of Bashan used to be known as the land of the Rephaites.
NLT.14: Jair, a leader from the tribe of Manasseh, conquered the whole Argob region in Bashan, all the way to the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites. Jair renamed this region after himself, calling it the Towns of Jair, as it is still known today.)
NLT.15: I gave Gilead to the clan of Makir.
NLT.16: But I also gave part of Gilead to the tribes of Reuben and Gad. The area I gave them extended from the middle of the Arnon Gorge in the south to the Jabbok River on the Ammonite frontier.
NLT.17: They also received the Jordan Valley, all the way from the Sea of Galilee down to the Dead Sea, with the Jordan River serving as the western boundary. To the east were the slopes of Pisgah.
NLT.18: “At that time I gave this command to the tribes that would live east of the Jordan: ‘Although the LORD your God has given you this land as your property, all your fighting men must cross the Jordan ahead of your Israelite relatives, armed and ready to assist them.
NLT.19: Your wives, children, and numerous livestock, however, may stay behind in the towns I have given you.
NLT.20: When the LORD has given security to the rest of the Israelites, as he has to you, and when they occupy the land the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan River, then you may all return here to the land I have given you.’
NLT.21: “At that time I gave Joshua this charge: ‘You have seen for yourself everything the LORD your God has done to these two kings. He will do the same to all the kingdoms on the west side of the Jordan.
NLT.22: Do not be afraid of the nations there, for the LORD your God will fight for you.’
NLT.23: “At that time I pleaded with the LORD and said,
NLT.24: ‘O Sovereign LORD, you have only begun to show your greatness and the strength of your hand to me, your servant. Is there any god in heaven or on earth who can perform such great and mighty deeds as you do?
NLT.25: Please let me cross the Jordan to see the wonderful land on the other side, the beautiful hill country and the Lebanon mountains.’
NLT.26: “But the LORD was angry with me because of you, and he would not listen to me. ‘That’s enough!’ he declared. ‘Speak of it no more.
NLT.27: But go up to Pisgah Peak, and look over the land in every direction. Take a good look, but you may not cross the Jordan River.
NLT.28: Instead, commission Joshua and encourage and strengthen him, for he will lead the people across the Jordan. He will give them all the land you now see before you as their possession.’
NLT.29: So we stayed in the valley near Beth-peor.

WEB.1: Then we turned, and went up the way to Bashan. Og the king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.
WEB.2: Yahweh said to me, “Don’t fear him; for I have delivered him, with all his people, and his land, into your hand. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.”
WEB.3: So Yahweh our God delivered into our hand Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people. We struck him until no one was left to him remaining.
WEB.4: We took all his cities at that time. There was not a city which we didn’t take from them; sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
WEB.5: All these were cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars; besides a great many villages without walls.
WEB.6: We utterly destroyed them, as we did to Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying every inhabited city, with the women and the little ones.
WEB.7: But all the livestock, and the plunder of the cities, we took for plunder for ourselves.
WEB.8: We took the land at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon.
WEB.9: (The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.)
WEB.10: We took all the cities of the plain, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, to Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
WEB.11: (For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the Rephaim. Behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron. Isn’t it in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? Nine cubits  was its length, and four cubits its width, after the cubit of a man.)
WEB.12: This land we took in possession at that time: from Aroer, which is by the valley of the Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead, and its cities, gave I to the Reubenites and to the Gadites:
WEB.13: and the rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, gave I to the half-tribe of Manasseh; all the region of Argob, even all Bashan. (The same is called the land of Rephaim.
WEB.14: Jair the son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob, to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and called them, even Bashan, after his own name, Havvoth Jair, to this day.)
WEB.16: To the Reubenites and to the Gadites I gave from Gilead even to the valley of the Arnon, the middle of the valley, and its border, even to the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon;
WEB.17: the Arabah also, and the Jordan and its border, from Chinnereth even to the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah eastward.
WEB.18: I commanded you at that time, saying, “Yahweh your God has given you this land to possess it. You shall pass over armed before your brothers the children of Israel, all the men of valor.
WEB.19: But your wives, and your little ones, and your livestock, (I know that you have much livestock), shall live in your cities which I have given you,
WEB.20: until Yahweh gives rest to your brothers, as to you, and they also possess the land which Yahweh your God gives them beyond the Jordan. Then you shall each return to his own possession, which I have given you.”
WEB.21: I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, “Your eyes have seen all that Yahweh your God has done to these two kings. So shall Yahweh do to all the kingdoms where you go over.
WEB.22: You shall not fear them; for Yahweh your God himself fights for you.”
WEB.23: I begged Yahweh at that time, saying,
WEB.24: “Lord  Yahweh, you have begun to show your servant your greatness, and your strong hand. For what god is there in heaven or in earth that can do works like yours, and mighty acts like yours?
WEB.25: Please let me go over and see the good land that is beyond the Jordan, that fine mountain, and Lebanon.”
WEB.26: But Yahweh was angry with me for your sakes, and didn’t listen to me. Yahweh said to me, “Let this satisfy you. Speak no more to me of this matter.
WEB.27: Go up to the top of Pisgah, and lift up your eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and see with your eyes; for you shall not go over this Jordan.
WEB.28: But commission Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him; for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which you shall see.”
WEB.29: So we stayed in the valley near Beth Peor.

AMP.1: "Then we turned and went up the road toward Bashan, and at Edrei, Og king of Bashan, with all his people came out to meet us in battle.
AMP.2: And the LORD said to me, 'Do not fear him, for I have handed him over to you, him and all his people and his land; and you shall do to him just as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.'
AMP.3: So the LORD our God also handed over Og king of Bashan, and all his people, into our hand and we struck him until no survivor was left.
AMP.4: We captured all his cities at that time; there was not a city which we did not take from them: sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
AMP.5: All these cities were fortified and unassailable with their high walls, gates, and bars; in addition, [there were] a very great number of unwalled villages.
AMP.6: We utterly destroyed them, just as we did to Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying every city—the men, women, and children.
AMP.7: But we took all the cattle and the spoil of the cities as plunder for ourselves.
AMP.8: "So we took the land at that time from the hand of the two kings [Sihon and Og] of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon
AMP.9: (the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir):
AMP.10: all the cities of the plain and all Gilead and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan."
AMP.11: (For only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the [the giants known as the] Rephaim. Behold, his bed frame was a bed frame of iron; is it not in Rabbah of the Ammonites? It was nine cubits (12 ft.) long and four cubits (6 ft.) wide, using the cubit of a man [the forearm to the end of the middle finger].)
AMP.12: "So we took possession of this land at that time. I gave the territory from Aroer, which is by the valley of the Arnon, along with half of the hill country of Gilead and its cities to the Reubenites and to the Gadites.
AMP.13: The rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh, that is, all the region of Argob (concerning all Bashan, it is called the land of Rephaim.
AMP.14: Jair the son (descendant) of Manasseh took all the region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, that is Bashan, and called it after his own name, Havvoth (the villages of) Jair, as it is called to this day.)
AMP.15: I gave Gilead to Machir [of Manasseh].
AMP.16: To the Reubenites and Gadites I gave the territory from Gilead as far as the Valley of Arnon, with the middle of the Valley as a boundary, and as far as the Jabbok River, the boundary of the sons of Ammon;
AMP.17: the Arabah also, with the Jordan as its boundary, from Chinnereth (the Sea of Galilee) as far as the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea (Dead Sea), at the foot of the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
AMP.18: "Then I commanded you [Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh] at that time, saying, 'The LORD your God has given you this land to possess; all you who are brave men shall cross over [the Jordan] armed before your brothers, the sons of Israel.
AMP.19: But your wives and your children and your cattle—I know that you have much livestock—shall remain in your cities which I have given you,
AMP.20: until the LORD gives rest to your fellow countrymen as [He has] to you, and they also possess the land which the LORD your God has given them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the land (possession) which I have given to you.'
AMP.21: I commanded Joshua at that time, saying, 'Your eyes have seen everything that the LORD your God has done to these two kings [Sihon and Og]; so the LORD shall do the same to all the kingdoms into which you are about to cross.
AMP.22: Do not fear them, for it is the LORD your God who is fighting for you.'
AMP.23: "Then I pleaded with the LORD at that time [for His favor], saying,
AMP.24: 'O Lord GOD, You have only begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your mighty hand; for what god is there in heaven or on earth that can do such works and mighty acts (miracles) as Yours?
AMP.25: I pray, let me go over and see the good land that is beyond the Jordan, that good hill country [with Hermon] and Lebanon.'
AMP.26: But the LORD was angry with me because of you [and your rebellion at Meribah], and would not listen to me; and the LORD said to me, 'Enough! Speak to Me no longer about this matter.
AMP.27: Go up to the top of [Mount] Pisgah and raise your eyes toward the west and north and south and east, and see it with your eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.
AMP.28: But command Joshua and encourage and strengthen him, for he shall go across and lead this people, and he will give them the land which you see as an inheritance.'
AMP.29: So we stayed in the Valley opposite Beth-peor.

NIV.1:
Defeat of Og King of Bashan
Next we turned and went up along the road toward Bashan, and Og king of Bashan with his whole army marched out to meet us in battle at Edrei.
NIV.2: The Lord said to me, “Do not be afraid of him, for I have handed him over to you with his whole army and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon.”
NIV.3: So the Lord our God also gave into our hands Og king of Bashan and all his army. We struck them down, leaving no survivors.
NIV.4: At that time we took all his cities. There was not one of the sixty cities that we did not take from them—the whole region of Argob, Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
NIV.5: All these cities were fortified with high walls and with gates and bars, and there were also a great many unwalled villages.
NIV.6: We completely destroyed them, as we had done with Sihon king of Heshbon, destroying every city—men, women and children.
NIV.7: But all the livestock and the plunder from their cities we carried off for ourselves.
NIV.8: So at that time we took from these two kings of the Amorites the territory east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Gorge as far as Mount Hermon.
NIV.9: (Hermon is called Sirion by the Sidonians; the Amorites call it Senir.)
NIV.10: We took all the towns on the plateau, and all Gilead, and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns of Og’s kingdom in Bashan.
NIV.11: (Only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaites. His bed was made of iron and was more than thirteen feet long and six feet wide. It is still in Rabbah of the Ammonites.)
NIV.12:
Division of the Land
Of the land that we took over at that time, I gave the Reubenites and the Gadites the territory north of Aroer by the Arnon Gorge, including half the hill country of Gilead, together with its towns.
NIV.13: The rest of Gilead and also all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh. (The whole region of Argob in Bashan used to be known as a land of the Rephaites.
NIV.14: Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites; it was named after him, so that to this day Bashan is called Havvoth Jair.)
NIV.15: And I gave Gilead to Makir.
NIV.16: But to the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the territory extending from Gilead down to the Arnon Gorge (the middle of the gorge being the border) and out to the Jabbok River, which is the border of the Ammonites.
NIV.17: Its western border was the Jordan in the Arabah, from Kinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah (the Salt Sea), below the slopes of Pisgah.
NIV.18: I commanded you at that time: “The Lord your God has given you this land to take possession of it. But all your able-bodied men, armed for battle, must cross over ahead of your brother Israelites.
NIV.19: However, your wives, your children and your livestock (I know you have much livestock) may stay in the towns I have given you,
NIV.20: until the Lord gives rest to your brothers as he has to you, and they too have taken over the land that the Lord your God is giving them, across the Jordan. After that, each of you may go back to the possession I have given you.”
NIV.21:
Moses Forbidden to Cross the Jordan
At that time I commanded Joshua: “You have seen with your own eyes all that the Lord your God has done to these two kings. The Lord will do the same to all the kingdoms over there where you are going.
NIV.22: Do not be afraid of them; the Lord your God himself will fight for you.”
NIV.23: At that time I pleaded with the Lord:
NIV.24: “O Sovereign Lord, you have begun to show to your servant your greatness and your strong hand. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do the deeds and mighty works you do?
NIV.25: Let me go over and see the good land beyond the Jordan—that fine hill country and Lebanon.”
NIV.26: But because of you the Lord was angry with me and would not listen to me. “That is enough,” the Lord said. “Do not speak to me anymore about this matter.
NIV.27: Go up to the top of Pisgah and look west and north and south and east. Look at the land with your own eyes, since you are not going to cross this Jordan.
NIV.28: But commission Joshua, and encourage and strengthen him, for he will lead this people across and will cause them to inherit the land that you will see.”
NIV.29: So we stayed in the valley near Beth Peor.

NET.1: Next we set out on the route to Bashan, but King Og of Bashan and his whole army came out to meet us in battle at Edrei.
NET.2: The LORD, however, said to me, “Don’t be afraid of him because I have already given him, his whole army, and his land to you. You will do to him exactly what you did to King Sihon of the Amorites who lived in Heshbon.”
NET.3: So the LORD our God did indeed give over to us King Og of Bashan and his whole army and we struck them down until not a single survivor was left.
NET.4: We captured all his cities at that time — there was not a town we did not take from them — sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the dominion of Og in Bashan.
NET.5: All of these cities were fortified by high walls, gates, and locking bars; in addition there were a great many open villages.
NET.6: We put all of these under divine judgment just as we had done to King Sihon of Heshbon — every occupied city, including women and children.
NET.7: But all the livestock and plunder from the cities we kept for ourselves.
NET.8: So at that time we took the land of the two Amorite kings in the Transjordan from Wadi Arnon to Mount Hermon
NET.9: (the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion and the Amorites call it Senir),
NET.10: all the cities of the plateau, all of Gilead and Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
NET.11: Only King Og of Bashan was left of the remaining Rephaites. (It is noteworthy that his sarcophagus was made of iron. Does it not, indeed, still remain in Rabbath of the Ammonites? It is thirteen and a half feet long and six feet wide according to standard measure.)
NET.12: This is the land we brought under our control at that time: The territory extending from Aroer by the Wadi Arnon and half the Gilead hill country with its cities I gave to the Reubenites and Gadites.
NET.13: The rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to half the tribe of Manasseh. (All the region of Argob, that is, all Bashan, is called the land of Rephaim.
NET.14: Jair, son of Manasseh, took all the Argob region as far as the border with the Geshurites and Maacathites (namely Bashan) and called it by his name, Havvoth-Jair, which it retains to this very day.)
NET.16: To the Reubenites and Gadites I allocated the territory extending from Gilead as far as Wadi Arnon (the exact middle of the wadi was a boundary) all the way to the Wadi Jabbok, the Ammonite border.
NET.17: The Arabah and the Jordan River were also a border, from the sea of Chinnereth to the sea of the Arabah (that is, the Salt Sea), beneath the watershed of Pisgah to the east.
NET.18: At that time I instructed you as follows: “The LORD your God has given you this land for your possession. You warriors are to cross over before your fellow Israelites equipped for battle.
NET.19: But your wives, children, and livestock (of which I know you have many) may remain in the cities I have given you.
NET.20: You must fight until the LORD gives your countrymen victory as he did you and they take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them on the other side of the Jordan River. Then each of you may return to his own territory that I have given you.”
NET.21: I also commanded Joshua at the same time, “You have seen everything the LORD your God did to these two kings; he will do the same to all the kingdoms where you are going.
NET.22: Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God will personally fight for you.”
NET.23: Moreover, at that time I pleaded with the LORD,
NET.24: “O, Lord GOD, you have begun to show me your greatness and strength. (What god in heaven or earth can rival your works and mighty deeds?)
NET.25: Let me please cross over to see the good land on the other side of the Jordan River — this good hill country and the Lebanon!”
NET.26: But the LORD was angry at me because of you and would not listen to me. Instead, he said to me, “Enough of that! Do not speak to me anymore about this matter.
NET.27: Go up to the top of Pisgah and take a good look to the west, north, south, and east, for you will not be allowed to cross the Jordan.
NET.28: Commission Joshua, and encourage and strengthen him, because he will lead these people over and will enable them to inherit the land you will see.”
NET.29: So we settled down in the valley opposite Beth Peor.
